verses.pali: Saṁyutta Nikāya 42.11
verses.english: Linked Discourses 42.11

verses.pali: 1. Gāmaṇivagga
verses.english: 1. Chiefs

verses.pali: Bhadrakasutta
verses.english: With Bhadraka

verses.pali: Ekaṁ samayaṁ bhagavā mallesu viharati uruvelakappaṁ nāma mallānaṁ nigamo.
verses.english: At one time the Buddha was staying in the land of the Mallas, near the Mallian town named Uruvelakappa.

verses.pali: Atha kho bhadrako gāmaṇi yena bhagavā tenupasaṅkami; upasaṅkamitvā bhagavantaṁ abhivādetvā ekamantaṁ nisīdi. Ekamantaṁ nisinno kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavantaṁ etadavoca:
verses.english: Then Bhadraka the village chief went up to the Buddha, bowed, sat down to one side, and said to him:

verses.pali: “sādhu me, bhante, bhagavā dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desetū”ti.
verses.english: “Please, sir, let the Blessed One teach me the origin and disappearance of suffering.”

verses.pali: “Ahañce te, gāmaṇi, atītamaddhānaṁ ārabbha dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṁ:
verses.english: “Chief, if I were to teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering in connection with the past, saying

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ ahosi atītamaddhānan’ti, tatra te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati.
verses.english: ‘this is how it was in the past,’ you might have doubts or uncertainties about that.

verses.pali: Ahañce te, gāmaṇi, anāgatamaddhānaṁ ārabbha dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca deseyyaṁ:
verses.english: If I were to teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering in connection with the future, saying

verses.pali: ‘evaṁ bhavissati anāgatamaddhānan’ti, tatrāpi te siyā kaṅkhā, siyā vimati.
verses.english: ‘this is how it will be in the future,’ you might have doubts or uncertainties about that.

verses.pali: Api cāhaṁ, gāmaṇi, idheva nisinno ettheva te nisinnassa dukkhassa samudayañca atthaṅgamañca desessāmi.
verses.english: Rather, chief, I will teach you about the origin and disappearance of suffering as I am sitting right here and you are sitting right there.

verses.pali: Taṁ suṇāhi, sādhukaṁ manasi karohi; bhāsissāmī”ti.
verses.english: Listen and apply your mind well, I will speak.”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”ti kho bhadrako gāmaṇi bhagavato paccassosi.
verses.english: “Yes, sir,” Bhadraka replied.

verses.pali: Bhagavā etadavoca:
verses.english: The Buddha said this:

verses.pali: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
verses.english: “What do you think, chief?

verses.pali: atthi te uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
verses.english: Are there any people here in Uruvelakappa who, if they were executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, it would cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

verses.pali: “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
verses.english: “There are, sir.”

verses.pali: “Atthi pana te, gāmaṇi, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
verses.english: “But are there any people here in Uruvelakappa who, if they were executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, it would not cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

verses.pali: “Atthi me, bhante, uruvelakappe manussā yesaṁ me vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
verses.english: “There are, sir.”

verses.pali: “Ko nu kho, gāmaṇi, hetu, ko paccayo yena te ekaccānaṁ uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
verses.english: “What’s the cause, chief, what’s the reason why, if this was to happen to some people it could cause you sorrow, while if it happens to others it does not?”

verses.pali: “Yesaṁ me, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, atthi me tesu chandarāgo.
verses.english: “The people regarding whom this would give rise to sorrow are those I have desire and passion.

verses.pali: Yesaṁ pana, bhante, uruvelakappiyānaṁ manussānaṁ vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā nuppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā, natthi me tesu chandarāgo”ti.
verses.english: The people regarding whom this would not give rise to sorrow are those I don’t have desire and passion.”

verses.pali: “Iminā tvaṁ, gāmaṇi, dhammena diṭṭhena viditena akālikena pattena pariyogāḷhena atītānāgate nayaṁ nehi:
verses.english: “With this present phenomenon that you have seen, understood, immediately attained, and fathomed, you can apply the same method to the past and future:

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kho kiñci atītamaddhānaṁ dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajji sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
verses.english: ‘All the suffering that arose in the past was rooted and sourced in desire.

verses.pali: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassa.
verses.english: For desire is the root of suffering.

verses.pali: Yampi hi kiñci anāgatamaddhānaṁ dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjissati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
verses.english: All the suffering that will arise in the future will be rooted and sourced in desire.

verses.pali: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’”ti.
verses.english: For desire is the root of suffering.’”

verses.pali: “Acchariyaṁ, bhante, abbhutaṁ, bhante.
verses.english: “It’s incredible, sir, it’s amazing!

verses.pali: Yāva subhāsitañcidaṁ, bhante, bhagavatā:
verses.english: How well said this was by the Buddha!

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
verses.english: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

verses.pali: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’ti.
verses.english: For desire is the root of suffering.’

verses.pali: Atthi me, bhante, ciravāsī nāma kumāro bahi āvasathe paṭivasati.
verses.english: I have a boy called Ciravāsi, who resides in a house away from here.

verses.pali: So khvāhaṁ, bhante, kālasseva vuṭṭhāya purisaṁ uyyojemi:
verses.english: I rise early and dispatch someone, saying:

verses.pali: ‘gaccha, bhaṇe, ciravāsiṁ kumāraṁ jānāhī’ti.
verses.english: ‘Go, I must say, and check on my boy Ciravāsi.’

verses.pali: Yāvakīvañca, bhante, so puriso nāgacchati, tassa me hoteva aññathattaṁ:
verses.english: Until they get back I worry:

verses.pali: ‘mā heva ciravāsissa kumārassa kiñci ābādhayitthā’”ti.
verses.english: ‘I hope nothing’s wrong with Ciravāsi!’”

verses.pali: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
verses.english: “What do you think, chief?

verses.pali: ciravāsissa kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
verses.english: If Ciravāsi was executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, would it cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

verses.pali: “Ciravāsissa me, bhante, kumārassa vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṁ, kiṁ pana me nuppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
verses.english: “How could it not, sir?”

verses.pali: “Imināpi kho etaṁ, gāmaṇi, pariyāyena veditabbaṁ:
verses.english: “This too is a way to understand:

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
verses.english: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

verses.pali: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’ti.
verses.english: For desire is the root of suffering.’

verses.pali: Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
verses.english: What do you think, chief?

verses.pali: yadā te ciravāsimātā adiṭṭhā ahosi, assutā ahosi, te ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā”ti?
verses.english: Before you’d seen or heard of Ciravāsi’s mother, did you have any desire or passion or fondness for her?”

verses.pali: “No hetaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “No, sir.”

verses.pali: “Dassanaṁ vā te, gāmaṇi, āgamma savanaṁ vā evaṁ te ahosi:
verses.english: “Then was it because you saw or heard of her that you had

verses.pali: ‘ciravāsimātuyā chando vā rāgo vā pemaṁ vā’”ti?
verses.english: desire or passion or fondness for her?”

verses.pali: “Evaṁ, bhante”.
verses.english: “Yes, sir.”

verses.pali: “Taṁ kiṁ maññasi, gāmaṇi,
verses.english: “What do you think, chief?

verses.pali: ciravāsimātuyā te vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā uppajjeyyuṁ sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti?
verses.english: If Ciravāsi’s mother was executed, imprisoned, fined, or condemned, would it cause you sorrow, lamentation, pain, sadness, and distress?”

verses.pali: “Ciravāsimātuyā me, bhante, vadhena vā bandhena vā jāniyā vā garahāya vā jīvitassapi siyā aññathattaṁ, kiṁ pana me nuppajjissanti sokaparidevadukkhadomanassupāyāsā”ti.
verses.english: “How could it not, sir?”

verses.pali: “Imināpi kho etaṁ, gāmaṇi, pariyāyena veditabbaṁ:
verses.english: “This too is a way to understand:

verses.pali: ‘yaṁ kiñci dukkhaṁ uppajjamānaṁ uppajjati, sabbaṁ taṁ chandamūlakaṁ chandanidānaṁ.
verses.english: ‘All the suffering that arises is rooted and sourced in desire.

verses.pali: Chando hi mūlaṁ dukkhassā’”ti.
verses.english: For desire is the root of suffering.’”

verses.pali: Ekādasamaṁ.
